packageRules.description: One PR for all action bumps; they are reviewed together anyway.

Our own features, published from this repo. They are referenced by major only, so every 1.x release is picked up at build time with no file change. A 2.x would be our own decision, made in the same commit that publishes it -- not something to be told about by a bot.

Fedora majors are decided by a human, because Renovate cannot tell which ones are safe. quay.io/fedora/fedora publishes numeric tags for unreleased versions, and the docker datasource just takes the highest: with 44 stable it proposed 46, which is rawhide -- Fedora's rolling development branch. 45 is a prerelease too. The bare :44 tag is still pulled fresh on every build, so rebuilds keep picking up Fedora 44 updates; only the jump to 45 or 46 is ours to make.
